## Shell lexer parity corpus.
##
## One command per line. A line beginning with `##` is a comment; empty lines
## are skipped. The two-character sequence \N stands for a newline byte, so a
## single corpus line can carry a multi-line command; every other backslash is
## passed through untouched.
##
## Everything above the %%DIVERGENT marker is asserted word-for-word against
## `shlex.split(line, posix=True)` — see tests/shlex_oracle.py, which turns
## this file into src/testdata/shell-oracle.jsonl, and the "shlex parity"
## test in src/shell.zig, which asserts against that.
##
## Lines that shlex REJECTS (an unterminated quote, a dangling escape) are
## still part of the asserted section: the oracle records the exception and
## the test asserts we set the matching signal instead of crashing.
##
## Below the marker are the cases where this lexer deliberately implements
## POSIX shell and shlex does not. Each one carries the reason.

## --- ordinary commands ---
ls
ls -la
echo hello world
/usr/bin/env
./script.sh arg1 arg2
git status
make -j4 all
printf %s done
tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C /tmp
curl -sSL https://example.com/path?a=1
grep -rn TODO src
cp -r a/b/c d/e/f
python3 script.py --flag value
node --experimental-vm-modules test.js
cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
zig build test
rm -rf ./build
mv old.txt new.txt
systemctl status nginx
journalctl -u nginx -n 100
ps aux
df -h /
du -sh .
head -n 20 file.txt
tail -f /var/log/syslog
wc -l file.txt
sort -u list.txt
uniq -c
cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd
tr a-z A-Z
date +%Y-%m-%d
rsync -av --delete src/ dst/
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces
/usr/local/bin/tool --help
ls ~/Documents
ls ../parent
ls ./relative
cat /etc/hosts

## --- single quotes ---
echo 'hello world'
echo 'it is'
echo ''
echo 'a b  c'
sed 's/a/b/g' file.txt
echo 'quoted "double" inside'
echo 'tab	inside'
echo 'back\slash'
echo '\'
echo ' '
awk '{print $1}' file
jq '.a.b' file.json
find . -name '*.txt' -type f
grep 'ñ' file.txt
echo 'don'\''t'
echo '$notexpanded'

## --- double quotes ---
echo "hello world"
echo ""
echo "a  b"
echo "it's"
echo "say \"hi\""
echo "back\\slash"
echo "keep\nliteral"
echo "path/to/file"
echo "$HOME/bin"
echo "${VAR}"
echo "a\"b"
echo "\\"
echo "  leading"
echo "	"
echo "multi word arg" second
printf "%s\n" value
echo "--flag=with space"
ls "/path with spaces/file"
psql -c "DROP TABLE users"
mysql -e "SELECT 1"
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.example.com

## --- adjacent quotes: concatenation ---
echo a"b"c
echo 'a'"b"'c'
echo pre"fix"post
echo ""empty
echo x''y
echo "a"'b'"c"d
echo abc"def"
echo "abc"def
echo ''''
echo a''b
echo a'b'c'd'e
echo ""''""
echo x"y z"w
echo "a b"'c d'
echo "'"
echo '"'

## --- empty arguments ---
cmd '' ''
cmd "" x
test -z ""
echo "" ""

## --- backslash escapes outside quotes ---
echo a\ b
echo \$HOME
echo \'quoted\'
echo \\
echo a\"b
echo one\ two three
cp file\ name.txt dest
echo \a
echo x\ty
\ls

## --- unicode ---
echo héllo wörld
echo "日本語 テスト"
echo 'Ünïcödé'
echo café-naïve
echo "emoji 🎉 here"
echo ✓ ✗

## --- whitespace forms ---
echo   spaced    out
	echo leading-tab
echo	tab	separated

## --- embedded newlines ---
echo a\Nb
echo "line1\Nline2"
echo 'l1\Nl2'
cmd one\Ncmd two

## --- expansions, passed through unevaluated ---
echo $VAR
echo $VAR/path
echo a$VAR b
echo "$@"
echo "$1 $2"
echo $-
echo ${#arr}
echo key=value
FOO=bar echo hi
A=1 B=2 env
echo --flag=value
echo -- --literal
echo -n

## --- `#` away from a word boundary is an ordinary byte ---
echo a#b
echo x#y#z

## --- wrappers (parity is over the outer word split only) ---
bash -lc "echo hi"
sh -c 'ls -la'
zsh -ic "true"
env A=1 B=2 sh
timeout 5 sleep 1
sudo -u www ls
nohup sleep 100
nice -n 10 make
uv run python -m pytest
npx prettier --write .
git -C /repo status
watch -n 5 df -h
ssh host "uptime"
docker run --rm -it alpine sh
xargs -0 rm
command ls
sed -e 's/x/y/' -e 's/a/b/' f
awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd
find . -name "*.zig"
jq -r '.items[] | .name' f.json

## --- shlex rejects these; we return a partial word plus a signal ---
echo "unterminated
echo 'unterminated
echo "mixed 'quotes
echo one "two three
echo trailing\

%%DIVERGENT

## Everything below is a DELIBERATE divergence from shlex. shlex.split is a
## word splitter with no grammar: it has no operators, no pipelines, no
## substitutions, no comments and no ANSI-C quoting, and (by design, since it
## is not a shell) it processes backslashes inside double quotes differently
## from POSIX. Assertions for these live in src/shell.zig's own tests.

## Operators. shlex emits `|`, `;`, `&&`, `>` and `2>&1` as ordinary word
## bytes; we split pipeline stages on them and attach redirections.
echo a | grep b
ls; pwd
a && b
a || b
cat f > out
cat f >> out
cmd 2>&1
cmd &> all.log
sleep 1 &
cmd1 && cmd2 | cmd3
(cd /x && ls)
{ ls; }

## Command substitution. shlex splits `$(date +%s)` into `$(date` and `+%s)`;
## we keep it as one word AND re-lex the inside as a nested command.
echo $(date)
echo $(date +%s)
echo `hostname`
echo "$(uname -a)"
diff <(sort a) <(sort b)

## ANSI-C quoting. shlex has no `$'...'` and yields a literal `$` plus the
## quoted bytes; we decode the escapes.
echo $'a\tb'
echo $'line\nbreak'
echo $'\x41\x42'

## Backslash inside double quotes. POSIX makes `\` special before $ ` " \ and
## newline only; shlex keeps the backslash before $ and ` as well.
echo "a\$b"
echo "a\`b"

## Line continuation. POSIX removes backslash-newline everywhere; shlex turns
## it into a literal newline inside the token.
echo a\\Nb
echo "a\\Nb"

## Comments. shlex.split(comments=False) treats `#` as an ordinary byte; a
## shell ends the line there.
## comment-only line
echo hi # trailing comment

## Heredocs. shlex has no notion of one; we attach the body to the redirect.
cat <<EOF\Nbody line\NEOF
python3 <<PY\Nprint(1)\NPY
cat <<<"here string"
